cs.name: Computer Science
cs.blurb: Make software that people use: logic, data structures, and shipping real apps.

nodes.title: Think like a programmer
nodes.learn: Variables, loops, conditionals and functions in Python. You learn to break a problem into small steps a computer can follow.
nodes.objective: Write a number-guessing game in Python that gives 'higher/lower' hints and counts tries.

res.name: CS50's Intro to Programming with Python

nodes.title: Data structures
nodes.learn: Lists, dictionaries, stacks and queues, plus a first feel for why some code is faster (big-O).
nodes.objective: Build a command-line to-do app that stores tasks in a dictionary and sorts them by due date.

nodes.title: Web foundations
nodes.learn: HTML for structure, CSS for style, JavaScript for behaviour. How a browser turns files into a page.
nodes.objective: Build and publish a personal homepage with an about section and one project.

nodes.title: Git & teamwork
nodes.learn: Version control with git: commits, branches, pull requests. How real teams build software together.
nodes.objective: Put one of your projects on GitHub with at least 5 meaningful commits and a README.

nodes.title: Discrete math
nodes.learn: Binary, logic, sets and simple proofs — the math university CS courses lean on most in first year.
nodes.objective: Convert 10 numbers between binary and decimal by hand and explain a truth table to a friend.

nodes.title: Ship a real app
nodes.learn: Planning, building and iterating on software with real users. Feedback beats guessing.
nodes.objective: Build an app someone else actually uses, then collect feedback from 3 users and make one fix.

res.name: The Odin Project: Full Stack JavaScript

mastery: Grow your app to 10 real users and track one usage number weekly.
Ship a version 2 based on that data and write a short postmortem.

cross.title: Tech entrepreneurship
cross.learn: Building an app is half a startup. The other half is customers, money and pitching.
cross.objective: Write a one-page lean canvas for your app.

nodes.title: Cybersecurity
nodes.learn: Security grows out of CS: you need to know how systems work before you can protect or break them.
nodes.objective: Watch the first CS50 Cybersecurity lecture and write 3 things that surprised you.

nodes.title: Data Science & AI
nodes.learn: Data science mixes CS with statistics to find patterns and build models that learn.
nodes.objective: Watch the first CS50 AI lecture and describe one real app that uses search or prediction.

res.name: CS50's Introduction to AI with Python

cyber.name: Cybersecurity
cyber.blurb: Defend networks, find vulnerabilities ethically, and think like an attacker to stop one.

nodes.title: Networking basics
nodes.learn: IP addresses, DNS, ports, TCP vs UDP. How a message actually crosses the internet.
nodes.objective: Draw a diagram of your home network (devices, router, internet) and label what each part does.

nodes.title: Linux command line
nodes.learn: Navigating files, permissions and processes from a terminal — the daily tool of security work.
nodes.objective: Beat OverTheWire Bandit levels 0 to 10.

nodes.title: Cryptography
nodes.learn: Ciphers, hashing and public-key encryption: how secrets stay secret online.
nodes.objective: Encrypt and decrypt a message with Caesar and Vigenère ciphers, then explain public-key crypto in 5 sentences.

nodes.title: Ethics & the law
nodes.learn: Authorization, responsible disclosure and computer-misuse laws. The line between a researcher and a criminal is permission.
nodes.objective: Write a one-page summary of responsible disclosure and your country's computer-misuse law.
mastery: Write a responsible-disclosure policy for a pretend school website.
Give a 5-minute talk on hacking ethics to a class or club.

cross.title: Cyber law & privacy
cross.learn: Privacy, breach and cybercrime laws are written by people who understand both technology and law.
cross.objective: Read the Privacy Commissioner's summary of PIPEDA and explain it in plain words.

nodes.title: Capture the Flag
nodes.learn: Legal hacking puzzles: web exploits, forensics, reverse engineering. Learn by breaking practice targets.
nodes.objective: Solve 10 picoCTF practice challenges across at least 3 categories.

nodes.title: Blue team defender
nodes.learn: Logs, alerts and incident response — the defensive side most security jobs start in.
nodes.objective: Complete an introductory SOC room on TryHackMe and write a short incident report.

data.name: Data Science & AI
data.blurb: Turn messy numbers into answers and models that predict what comes next.

nodes.title: Statistics foundations
nodes.learn: Mean, median, spread, distributions and why a sample can lie.
nodes.objective: Survey 20 classmates on one question and summarize the results with a chart and two statistics.

nodes.title: Spreadsheets & SQL
nodes.learn: Asking questions of tables: filtering, grouping and joining data.
nodes.objective: Finish all SQLBolt lessons and answer 5 of your own questions with queries.

nodes.title: Python for data
nodes.learn: pandas for cleaning data and plotting libraries for charts.
nodes.objective: Clean a public Kaggle dataset and make 3 charts that each answer a question.

nodes.title: Math for models
nodes.learn: Vectors, matrices and slopes — the intuition behind how models learn.
nodes.objective: Explain in your own words, with a sketch, what a gradient is and why it points uphill.

nodes.title: Machine learning
nodes.learn: Training, testing and overfitting. Decision trees and how to measure a model honestly.
nodes.objective: Train a model on the Kaggle Titanic dataset and beat 75% accuracy.

res.name: Kaggle Learn: Intro to Machine Learning

nodes.title: Data story capstone
nodes.learn: Communicating findings so non-experts can act on them.
nodes.objective: Publish an analysis of a local issue (transit, sports, weather) with 3 charts and a clear conclusion.
mastery: Get feedback from someone affected by your issue and revise the analysis.
Present your data story to a local group, council meeting or school board.

cross.title: Policy analysis
cross.learn: Policy analysts use data to shape laws and public programs.
cross.objective: Find a Statistics Canada table tied to a current policy debate and summarize what it shows.

health.name: Health Sciences
health.blurb: Pre-med, nursing, pharmacy and more: science in service of people.

nodes.title: Biology & chemistry core
nodes.learn: Cells, DNA, chemical reactions — the base every health program builds on.
nodes.objective: Finish one Khan Academy biology unit and score 80%+ on its unit test.

nodes.title: Anatomy & physiology
nodes.learn: How the body's systems work together, from the heart to the nervous system.
nodes.objective: Make labelled diagrams of 5 body systems and explain one disease affecting each.

nodes.title: First aid & CPR
nodes.learn: Responding to emergencies: assessment, CPR and AED use. Most care roles expect this certificate.
nodes.objective: Earn a first aid & CPR certificate.

nodes.title: Volunteer in care
nodes.learn: What patient care actually feels like day to day. Admissions committees look for this.
nodes.objective: Volunteer 20 hours at a hospital, clinic or seniors' home and write a one-page reflection.

nodes.title: Reading research
nodes.learn: How to read a study: sample size, controls and why one paper isn't proof.
nodes.objective: Find one study on PubMed and summarize its question, method and limits in plain language.
mastery: Compare two studies that disagree and explain why they might differ.
Write a plain-language evidence summary a family member could use.

cross.title: Health policy & law
cross.learn: Evidence becomes rules through health policy and law: consent, privacy, public health orders.
cross.objective: Pick one Canadian public health policy and trace the evidence behind it.

nodes.title: Shadow a professional
nodes.learn: Comparing real careers: doctor, nurse, pharmacist, physiotherapist, paramedic.
nodes.objective: Job-shadow or interview a health professional and compare their path with one other role.

nodes.title: Health data & bioinformatics
nodes.learn: Hospitals and labs generate huge datasets; analysts who understand biology are rare and needed.
nodes.objective: Read about bioinformatics and list 3 problems it helps solve.

eng.name: Engineering
eng.blurb: Design, build and test physical things — from phone stands to robots.

nodes.title: Physics of motion
nodes.learn: Forces, energy and Newton's laws: why bridges stand and eggs break.
nodes.objective: Build an egg-drop device from 2 metres and calculate the impact force with and without it.

nodes.title: CAD & 3D design
nodes.learn: Computer-aided design: sketches, extrusions, tolerances.
nodes.objective: Design a phone stand in CAD and export a printable STL file.

nodes.title: Electronics & Arduino
nodes.learn: Circuits, voltage, sensors and microcontrollers.
nodes.objective: Build (or simulate in Tinkercad Circuits) a circuit where a sensor controls an LED.

nodes.title: Design process
nodes.learn: Define, ideate, prototype, test, repeat — how engineers solve messy real problems.
nodes.objective: Document all 5 stages while fixing one real annoyance at home or school.
mastery: Run a second design cycle on the same problem using user feedback, and measure the improvement.
Mentor a younger student through a full design cycle, or enter a design competition.

cross.title: Patent & tech law
cross.learn: Engineers who understand law become patent agents and tech lawyers: they decide who owns an invention.
cross.objective: Look up how patents work in Canada and summarize what an inventor must prove.

nodes.title: Robotics
nodes.learn: Mechanics, electronics and code working as one machine.
nodes.objective: Join a FIRST team or build a line-following robot.

nodes.title: Software for machines
nodes.learn: Embedded and robotics software sits right between engineering and CS.
nodes.objective: Write a program that reads a sensor and makes a decision based on it.

design.name: UX & Visual Design
design.blurb: Make products people love using: research, visuals, prototypes and accessibility.

nodes.title: Visual design basics
nodes.learn: Colour, typography, layout and hierarchy — why some posters work and others don't.
nodes.objective: Redesign one school poster three different ways and explain which works best.

nodes.title: User research
nodes.learn: Interviews and observation: designing from what people do, not what you assume.
nodes.objective: Interview 3 people about an app they find annoying and list their top pain points.
mastery: Run a usability test with 5 people on an existing app and rank the problems.
Turn your interviews into a persona and journey map and present them.

cross.title: Product management
cross.learn: Product managers decide what gets built and why. User research is their core skill.
cross.objective: Write a one-page requirements doc for a single feature.

nodes.title: Prototyping in Figma
nodes.learn: Wireframes, components and clickable prototypes.
nodes.objective: Make a clickable 5-screen prototype that fixes one pain point you found.

nodes.title: Accessibility
nodes.learn: Designing for everyone: contrast, screen readers, keyboard use (WCAG).
nodes.objective: Audit a website with WAVE and propose fixes for 3 issues.

nodes.title: Portfolio case study
nodes.learn: Telling the story of a design: problem, research, iterations, result.
nodes.objective: Write a case study for your prototype with before/after screens.

nodes.title: Front-end development
nodes.learn: Designers who can code their own prototypes become front-end developers.
nodes.objective: Rebuild one of your Figma screens in HTML and CSS.

law.name: Law & Policy
law.blurb: Argue, research and shape the rules society runs on.

nodes.title: How law works
nodes.learn: Courts, statutes, common law and Quebec's civil law, and where the Charter fits.
nodes.objective: Watch a public court or tribunal hearing (many are streamed) and summarize each side's argument.

res.name: Justice Canada: Canada's System of Justice

nodes.title: Argument & debate
nodes.learn: Building a case: claims, evidence, rebuttal, and persuading a neutral listener.
nodes.objective: Compete in a debate or write a one-page persuasive brief on a school policy.

nodes.title: Legal research
nodes.learn: Finding and reading real decisions: facts, issue, ruling, reasoning.
nodes.objective: Find a Supreme Court of Canada decision on CanLII and summarize it in plain words.
mastery: Brief a case: facts, issue, decision and reasoning.
Write a 2-page legal memo answering a real question.

cross.title: Legal tech
cross.learn: Legal tech builds tools that make law searchable and accessible to everyone.
cross.objective: Search CanLII for 5 cases on one topic and describe a tool that would make it easier.

nodes.title: Rights & ethics
nodes.learn: Charter rights, their limits, and the ethics lawyers must follow.
nodes.objective: Write a short op-ed on a current Charter issue, presenting both sides fairly.

res.name: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms

nodes.title: Mock trial
nodes.learn: Courtroom roles, examination of witnesses and closing arguments.
nodes.objective: Take part in a mock trial as counsel or a witness.

nodes.title: Road to law school
nodes.learn: In most of Canada law is a second-entry degree: an undergrad in any field, the LSAT, then a JD.
nodes.objective: Compare admission requirements at 3 law schools and pick an undergrad that keeps the door open.

biz.name: Business & Entrepreneurship
biz.blurb: Start ventures, manage money and lead teams.

nodes.title: Money basics
nodes.learn: Revenue, costs, profit and budgeting.
nodes.objective: Build a one-month budget for a real or imagined small business.

nodes.title: Marketing
nodes.learn: Audiences, messaging and measuring whether a campaign worked.
nodes.objective: Market a school club event and measure turnout against a goal.

nodes.title: Accounting basics
nodes.learn: Income statements and balance sheets: the language of business.
nodes.objective: Build an income statement for a small venture scenario.

nodes.title: Pitch & sell
nodes.learn: Pitching an idea clearly and handling tough questions.
nodes.objective: Pitch an idea to 3 adults and write down their feedback.

nodes.title: Run a mini venture
nodes.learn: Running something real: sourcing, pricing, selling and tracking results.
nodes.objective: Run a small venture (bake sale, tutoring, reselling) and record revenue and costs.
mastery: Run the venture again and improve your profit margin.
Teach someone else to run it and write your playbook.

cross.title: Business analytics
cross.learn: Analysts turn sales and customer data into decisions.
cross.objective: Track your venture's sales in a spreadsheet and chart the trend.

nodes.title: Choose a business path
nodes.learn: Commerce, co-op and entrepreneurship programs, and how they differ.
nodes.objective: Compare 3 commerce programs, including co-op options.
